evidence.claim: Energy +10% in Oct as a top rotation destination
evidence.relation: rotation inflow on top of the oil supply bid

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Will Rising Long Term Rates Crash Stocks? (Sep 14)
evidence.claim: Rates rise with inflation, and energy/commodity stocks did very well in that regime this year — the rate-up/inflation-up pairing is a tailwind for the energy complex (though he avoids the sector long-run as unpredictable and volatile)
evidence.relation: inflation-driven rate rise → commodity revenue tailwind

evidence.source: Adam Khoo — The stock market has been choppy in the first quarter of 2026... (2026-04-15)
evidence.claim: The S&P 500 is down only about 9% YTD because it is 'held up by the energy stocks', while many quality stocks (Microsoft, Nvidia, Meta, Palo Alto) are down double digits or 20-30%. His reason: 'Oil goes up, energy companies make a lot of money.'
evidence.relation: Higher oil prices lift energy-company earnings, so energy has been supporting the index while tech and growth sectors fall. This is a current-regime flow and earnings effect that continues while oil stays elevated. He calls the period a 'bizarro' year, so persistence is uncertain.

resolution: The ceasefire leg (65.6 up-prob) rolled off with the Nov market and WTI dip-under-$90 odds firmed 63% → 66%, flipping the raw prior from 55.1 to a bearish-leaning 42.3. Khoo's October-rotation leg (lr 1.13, age 1) and the Sep-14 rate-up/inflation-up mechanism (decayed lr_eff 1.11, age 50) add up-evidence that lifts the posterior to 47.9 — neutral (low confidence), genuinely two-sided. The bullish tilt that combined the oil-supply bid with the geopolitical tail is gone; revisit if the ceasefire market returns with break odds over 55% (tail reattaches) or if dip-under-$90 odds firm past the 45% revision floor (bear lean dominates).
